name: Porto Alegre-Salgado Filho International Airport
before:
The airport for Porto Alegre and the wider metropolitan area sits 9 km from the city centre, which makes it one of the easier Brazilian arrivals to plan around. A people mover has connected the terminal to the metro network since 2013, and from the airport metro station most of the surrounding cities are reachable without changing to a taxi. Bus routes T5, T11 and B09 also run between Terminal 1 and the city.

It is operated by Fraport Brasil and has carried the name of Joaquim Pedro Salgado Filho, the senator who became Brazil's first Air Force minister, since 1951.

One thing worth knowing when looking at historic schedules: the airport did not run normally through much of 2024. There were no flights at all between 4 and 26 May, and from late May until 20 October services moved to Canoas Air Force Base with restrictions. Anything compared against that period will not reflect how the airport usually works.
after:
The airport for Porto Alegre and the wider metropolitan area sits 9 km from the city centre. City bus routes T5 and T11 run to the airport.

It is operated by Fraport Brasil and has carried the name of Joaquim Pedro Salgado Filho, Brazil's first Air Force minister and later a senator, since 1951.

One thing worth knowing when looking at historic schedules: the airport did not run normally through much of 2024. There were no flights at all between 4 and 26 May, and from late May until 20 October services moved to Canoas Air Force Base with restrictions. Flights returned to the airport on 21 October, with full operations from 16 December. Anything compared against that period will not reflect how the airport usually works.

claims.inAfter: Flights returned to the airport on 21 October, with full operations from 16 December.
claims.note: The old text implied normal service from 21 October. From then until 16 December the airport ran domestic flights only, on part of the runway, up to 128 a day between 8am and 10pm; the full 3.2 km runway, 24-hour operation and the return of international flights (from January 2025) followed on 16 December 2024. Fraport's live history page confirms the October 2024 reopening.

claims.claim: people mover to the metro since 2013; surrounding cities by metro
claims.wasBefore: A people mover has connected the terminal to the metro network since 2013, and from the airport metro station most of the surrounding cities are reachable without changing to a taxi.
claims.why: Not confirmed as running since the May 2024 floods, and a transport link needs a source from the last 12 months. Trensurb, which runs the people mover (Aeromóvel) and the metro, timed out and then answered 502; Correio do Povo, GZH and G1 all answer 'Blocked by egress policy', so no other tool tried them; Panrotas's search path does not exist; the operator's site has no transport page. A lead only, not evidence: Correio do Povo's own search listing (read with the link lister before its pages proved blocked) shows a headline of 11 May 2026 saying the Aeromóvel's repair, R$ 38 million over up to 12 months, has been added to the federal PAC programme, which suggests it is still out of service. For Andy to check by hand.

claims.why: B09 is not on Carris's list and rests on Wikipedia alone; 'Terminal 1' is an old name, as all airlines have used the one passenger terminal since September 2019 (operator). T5 and T11 are kept.

claims.wasBefore: the senator who became Brazil's first Air Force minister
claims.why: Wrong order: minister 1941 to 1945, senator 1947 to 1950 (FGV CPDOC). Corrected.
